kind.description: What class of output this fetcher produces. `evidence` (the default) writes a JSON payload the runner wraps in the evidence envelope and the paramify_evidence uploader attaches to an evidence set. `issue_report` writes the source tool's own file (a scan report) UNMODIFIED into <run>/issue-reports/, where the paramify_issues uploader posts it to an assessment intake. Issue reports are never enveloped: Paramify's intake parser reads the vendor's own structure, so anything added to the file breaks it.

timeout.description: Max seconds the runner lets a single invocation run before killing it and marking it failed. Defaults to 600. Raise it for long scanners (e.g. SSL Labs).

type.description: Output format. For an issue_report fetcher this is the format the source tool emits, and is the single source for the MIME type the uploader sends (xml and nessus are the scan-report formats; Paramify's intake accepts csv, json, xml, and nessus).

aggregation.description: How fanout outputs combine. per_target = one envelope per target invocation; aggregate = one combined envelope from a single invocation that receives the whole target list. Only meaningful when supports_targets is true.

required.description: False declares a credential the fetcher CAN use but does not need — the ambient-identity case, where a credential chain also accepts static keys. An optional secret the manifest omits is simply not injected.

description.description: What this credential is and when to supply it. Shown in `paramify describe` and the TUI.

per_target.description: If true, this secret is provided per-target during fanout (different value per target invocation). Only meaningful when supports_targets is true.

config_schema.description: Non-secret config knobs this fetcher accepts. Each value declares a field; when it has an `env`, the runner injects the resolved value as that env var. Platform-wide config lives in fetchers/_categories/<category>.yaml instead.

target_schema.description: When supports_targets is true, describes the shape of each target entry the runner will pass in. Free-form for v0.x; the runner will formalize validation when it lands.

evidence_set.description: Paramify evidence-set identity for this fetcher (1 fetcher = 1 evidence set). Fetcher-knowledge — what this evidence is and how it's collected — so it ships with the fetcher and is the shipped default the runner carries into the envelope. Customers override reference_id per program in the uploader config; they never edit this. Do NOT add controls/solution_capabilities here — that linkage stays Paramify-side. See docs/uploader_design.md.

reference_id.description: Stable idempotency key the uploader get-or-creates the evidence set by (e.g. EVD-OKTA-PHISHING-MFA).

instructions.description: How this evidence is collected (e.g. the API calls / commands). Written once into the evidence set on create.

description.description: Evidence-set description. Defaults to the fetcher's top-level description when omitted.

issue_report.description: Paramify assessment-intake identity for a `kind: issue_report` fetcher — the analogue of `evidence_set`, and equally fetcher-knowledge. Deliberately holds no assessmentId: which assessment a report goes to is a per-customer choice that lives in the manifest (`config.assessment_id`, written by `paramify assessments select`). See docs/issue_report_fetchers.md.

assessment_type.description: Which kind of Paramify assessment this report feeds. Used to filter the assessment picker, so a CSPM fetcher can only be pointed at a CONFIGURATION assessment and a vulnerability scanner at a VULNERABILITY one.

title.description: Artifact display title in Paramify. Defaults to the source filename when omitted. Per-target runs get the target identifier appended.

ksis.description: FedRAMP Key Security Indicators this fetcher's evidence speaks to (1 or more). Intrinsic to the fetcher, not a per-customer control mapping (those stay Paramify-side).

validators.description: Regex checks over this fetcher's evidence that show the control is being implemented (collection-side assertions, not per-customer compliance judgment). Each regex is matched against the fetcher's evidence payload.

allOf.$comment: The two kinds have disjoint identity blocks, and mixing them is always a mistake worth failing discovery over: an issue_report fetcher with an evidence_set would be silently ignored by both uploaders, and an evidence fetcher with an issue_report block would never reach an assessment.
Paramify's assessment intake accepts only these four formats, so an issue_report fetcher declaring html has no path to upload.
